extracted.intended_audience: architects, architectural historians, designers, and students of art/architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and descriptive standards for judging whether architecture is 'living' (vital, progressive) versus 'dead' (stagnant, lifeless). Focuses on imitation, execution, proportion, variety, and the treatment of borrowed elements with examples largely from Romanesque and early Gothic Italian architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation is not deadness except when unthinking
rubrics_metrics.description: It is no sign of deadness in a present art that it borrows or imitates, but only if it borrows without paying interest, or if it imitates without choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept imitation when it is selective and assimilated; condemn mere mechanical copying. Anti-pattern: slavish replication of precedent with no transformation or discernment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vital imitation has Frankness and Audacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Two distinguishing characters of vital imitation are its Frankness and its Audacity. Frankness: there is never any effort to conceal the degree of the sources of its borrowing. Audacity: unhesitating and sweeping sacrifice of precedent where precedent becomes inconvenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Raffaelle carrying a figure from Masaccio or borrowing from Perugino with openness; Romanesque architects gathering columns and capitals as they could find them. Audacity example: the Pisan solution of continuing column ranges into pedimental space, shortening shafts until only capitals remain. Positive sign when the borrower openly acknowledges source and boldly transforms it rather than hides it. Anti-patterns: secretive plagiarism or timid imitation that merely pastiches the source without transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frankness/Audacity are not excuses for repetition or unwise innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Frankness is in itself no excuse for repetition, nor Audacity for innovation, when the one is indolent and the other unwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish energetic, creative reuse from lazy repetition. Innovation must be thoughtful; audacious departures from precedent are valuable only when wise and purposeful. Anti-patterns: repetition presented as 'frank' borrowing; reckless novelty that disregards coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of execution to conception (neglect of refinement as sign of vitality)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain neglect or contempt of refinement in execution, or a visible subordination of execution to conception, is a sign of a progressive (living) art. Perfect and most delicate finish are right in their place, but progressive finish belongs to progressive art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage deliberate lack of over-finish in subordinate or exploratory work so conception remains primary. Expect perfect finish only where the art is 'perfected.' Anti-pattern: workmanship that has gone ahead of the design; overworked details that swamp the idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workmanship must not outrun design
rubrics_metrics.description: A fatal sign of stupor in an undeveloped art is that it had been taken aback by its own execution, and that the workmanship had gone ahead of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether fine execution is supporting a strong idea or merely masking weakness. If execution dominates and the design is secondary or absent, regard this as deadness. Scoring note: penalize pieces where finish outweighs conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impatience and contempt of minor handling as positive energy
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period when ground is being recovered, marks of intense impatience, a struggle toward something unattained, cause minor points of handling to be neglected and a restless disdain of qualities that appear contented or require time and care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize purposeful impatience—neglect of exact symmetry or minute finishing—that indicates vigorous development. Anti-pattern: slovenliness without purpose; aimless carelessness rather than energetic pursuit of new form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for asymmetry and unequal measurement as a living quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Contempt of exact symmetry and measurement, unequal measurements of even important features professing to be symmetrical, and curious variations in proportions are characteristic of living architecture and relieve severity of law by grace and suddenness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value subtle inequalities that achieve a pleasing whole (examples: Pisa west front with alternating proportional scheme; San Giovanni Evangelista variations). Anti-pattern: forced, mechanical symmetry that yields sterility; over-regularization that kills variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformative integration of borrowed fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: The architect who is quick in admiration and ready in imitation yet so strong in his own instincts that he reconstructs and re-arranges every fragment that he copies or borrows into harmony with his own thoughts — this reconstructive, transformative use is a majestic sign of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge borrowing by whether fragments are fused into a new, coherent whole (likened to blocks of unsubdued rock fused into lava). Anti-pattern: inserting borrowed pieces unchanged and subordinating the new work to them; lack of unifying intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective, light execution (sculptural sketching) in subordinate parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Subordinate portions may be worked with what appears at first slovenliness but is sculptural sketching—light execution that avoids sharp lines or over-precision so as not to draw the eye from the main composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize intentional, painterly/light handling of secondary elements (example: pulpit of St. Andrea at Pistoja — arch mouldings executed to disappear intermittently). Anti-pattern: uniformly sharp finish that distracts or competes with principal forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensation, accommodation, and organic variation define 'Living Architecture'
rubrics_metrics.description: Living Architecture: there is sensation in every inch of it, and an accommodation to every architectural necessity, with a determined variation in arrangement exactly like the related proportions and provisions in the structure of organic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess buildings for pervasive feeling, purposeful responses to functional constraints, and varied proportioning that reads as an organic whole. Examples: Pisa and San Giovanni structures whose subtle alternations and accommodations create continuous life. Anti-pattern: designs lacking sensation or any local responses, appearing rigid and mechanical.
